findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap arithmetic holds on the quoted figures: GBP 1300 x 12 = GBP 15,600 a year, divided by 52 and multiplied by 5 gives GBP 1,500.00. The GBP 1,500 deposit equals the cap and does not exceed it. Nothing in the contract contradicts this; s5 and s6 give no sign that the rent or deposit covers anything but the whole tenancy. The cap only applies to covered tenancies. Jurisdiction and tenancy type are both "unknown" in the context, so England and an ordinary private tenancy are assumed, not shown (s2 gives a London address, but that is not an express jurisdiction answer). This is therefore an amount-cap pass limited to the quoted figures. It says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. It stays conditional until the jurisdiction and tenancy scope are confirmed. No substantive counter-evidence defeats it. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

expectations.explanation: The output preserves the uncertainty about payment timing and payee. Finding emotion_classifier:stated_facts records that the due date and account are unconfirmed and the viewing is not arranged, without claiming a pre-viewing demand. act_payment_method asks how and when the deposit is paid, to which named account, and only after a viewing. message_checker question 0 asks whether and when payment has been requested.

No output asserts an immediate payment demand or pressure. The no_pressure check is cleared on the agent's own statement 'Do not send money while those details are missing'. The 0.6 clearing confidence is somewhat generous, but that is not the prohibited inference.

forbidden_assertions.explanation: No output says a bank transfer alone proves fraud. It is described neutrally as a mentioned payment method.
Timing is treated as unknown and framed as questions. No output says payment before viewing was demanded.
No output says the payee is verified. The payment_safety check stays unverified and the action asks for the named account.
The output says the viewing is not yet arranged, and message_checker asks whether a viewing has been offered. No output claims a viewing was completed.

unsupported_claims.output_quote: The agent explicitly takes time pressure off, and no pressure language was found.
unsupported_claims.explanation: The cited quote only says not to send money while details are missing. It does not explicitly give the student time to decide, so the 'explicitly takes time pressure off' framing slightly overstates it.

unsupported_claims.output_quote: £1,300 a month against roughly £950 for a room in W12 (approximate area figure): about 37% higher.
unsupported_claims.explanation: The area figure has no controlled source in the supplied data. It is labelled approximate, but it is unsupported by the evidence.

grounding_issues.explanation: The quote is verbatim, but it supports 'do not pay yet' rather than 'the agent gives you time to decide'. The claim is a loose interpretation.
The evidence_id 'listing' is a structured-source rendering that matches the listing rent. The claimed £950 area average has no support in any supplied source.

grading.reviewer_note: The deposit_cap finding is correctly conditional and states that it does not verify deposit protection. Companies House returned 503, which establishes nothing about the company. act_company_number appropriately asks for the number and does not infer non-existence. The deterministic audit shows all quotes match.
